Rashi on Gittin 5b:10:1.english: And do you understand [it so]? - That this is the case?

Rashi on Gittin 5b:10:2.hebrew: והא - מדסיימינן לעיל דריב"ל הוא דאמר "לפי שאין בקיאין", מכלל דרבי יוחנן, בר פלוגתיה דלעיל, אמר משום "לקיימו". והכא סיימינן דר' יוחנן הוא דאמר "בפני שנים":
Rashi on Gittin 5b:10:2.english: But - Since we concluded above that it is Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi who said "because they are not experts," it follows that Rabbi Yoḥanan, his disputant above, said [the reason is] "in order to ratify it." But here we concluded that it is Rabbi Yoḥanan who said "in the presence of two."

Rashi on Gittin 5b:11:1.hebrew: ועוד הא רבה אית ליה דרבא - ואפילו למ"ד "לפי שאין בקיאין לשמה", אית ליה נמי "לקיימו", וניבעי תלתא:
Rashi on Gittin 5b:11:1.english: And furthermore, Rabba holds [also] like Rava - And even according to the one who says [that the reason is] "because they are not experts in [writing it] for its own sake," he also holds [the reason] "to ratify it," and we should require three.

Rashi on Gittin 5b:12:1.hebrew: בשליח נעשה עד ועד נעשה דיין קמיפלגי - כלומר, אי אמרינן: כי היכי דשליח נעשה עד, הכי נמי עד נעשה דיין — קמיפלגי:
Rashi on Gittin 5b:12:1.english: In [the question of whether] an agent becomes a witness, and a witness becomes a judge, they disagree - That is, they disagree about whether we say that just as an agent becomes a witness, so too a witness becomes a judge.

Rashi on Gittin 5b:12:2.hebrew: מ"ד בפני שנים קסבר - כי היכי דשליח נעשה עד, ה"נ עד נעשה דיין. הלכך, מצטרף בהדייהו, והוו תלתא:
Rashi on Gittin 5b:12:2.english: The one who says [it must be] in the presence of two holds - Just as an agent becomes a witness, so too a witness becomes a judge. Therefore, he joins with them, and they are three.

Rashi on Gittin 5b:12:3.hebrew: ומ"ד בפני שלשה קסבר - אף ששליח נעשה עד, אין עד נעשה דיין:
Rashi on Gittin 5b:12:3.english: And the one who says [it must be] before three, holds - That even though an agent becomes a witness, a witness does not become a judge.

Rashi on Gittin 5b:13:1.hebrew: הכי גרסינן והא קיימא לן בדרבנן דעד נעשה דיין - כגון גבי קיום שטרות. אמרינן בכתובות (שם): שלשה שישבו לקיים את השטר, וקרא ערעור על אחד מהם כו', והוינן בה: למימרא דעד נעשה דיין כו', ומותבינן ומשנינן: ה"מ בעדות החדש דאורייתא, אבל בדרבנן עד נעשה דיין:
Rashi on Gittin 5b:13:1.english: This is how we read: But don't we maintain with regard to rabbinic law that a witness can become a judge - For example, with regard to the ratification of documents. We say in Ketubot (there): Three who sat to ratify the document, and a challenge was raised against one of them, etc. And we asked about it: Is this to say that a witness can become a judge, etc.? And we objected and answered: This applies only to the testimony of the new moon, which is by Torah law; but in rabbinic matters, a witness can become a judge.

Rashi on Gittin 5b:14:1.hebrew: כיון דאשה כשירה כו' - אי מכשרת בשנים, זמנין דמייתא ליה אשה וסמכינן עלה לאכשורי נמי בשנים, ואשה לא חזיא לאצטרופי בהדייהו לתלתא:
Rashi on Gittin 5b:14:1.english: Since a woman is fit, etc. - If it is valid with two, sometimes a woman will bring it to him, and we would rely on her to validate it with two as well, but a woman is not fit to join with them to make three.

Rashi on Gittin 5b:16:1.english: He must divorce her - the one who married her on the basis of this bill of divorce.

Rashi on Gittin 5b:18:1.hebrew: משום דלא אמר (לה) יוציא - בתמיה: והא גט כשר הוא, ובפניו נכתב! ומשום דלא אמר, הוי ולד ממזר?:
Rashi on Gittin 5b:18:1.english: Merely because he did not say [to her], he must divorce her - [This is stated] as an astonished question: But it is a valid bill of divorce, and it was written in his presence! And merely because he did not say so, the offspring is a *mamzer*?

Rashi on Gittin 5b:1:1.hebrew: טעמא מאי כו' דילמא אתי בעל מערער - דטעמא מאי אמור רבנן, דבעי למימר "דילמא אתי בעל ומערער". הילכך, אם לא ניסת — לא תינשא; אבל השתא דניסת, אמאי לפקה? אכתי לא אתי בעל ומערער — אנן ניקום ונערער:
Rashi on Gittin 5b:1:1.english: What is the reason, etc. Perhaps the husband will come and contest - What is the reason the Rabbis said [this requirement], that [the Gemara] wants to say "perhaps the husband will come and contest"? Therefore, if she has not [yet] married, she should not marry; but now that she has married, why should she leave [her husband]? The husband has still not come and contested — shall we arise and contest?

Rashi on Gittin 5b:1:2.hebrew: ואיבעית אימא: לא גרסינן. אלא הכי גרסינן: אלא להקל עליה, טעמא מאי וכו':
Rashi on Gittin 5b:1:2.english: And if you wish, say: We do not read [it that way]. Rather, this is how we read: "Rather, to be lenient with her, what is the reason?" etc.

Rashi on Gittin 5b:20:1.hebrew: אתא לקמיה דרבי אחי - באותה העיר שהיו כותבין אותו:
Rashi on Gittin 5b:20:1.english: He came before Rabbi Achai - In that city where they were writing it.

Rashi on Gittin 5b:20:2.hebrew: ממונה אגיטי - דקי"ל (קידושין דף ו:) כל שאינו יודע בטיב גיטין וקידושין לא יהא לו עסק עמהן, והוו ממנו גברא רבה לאורויי היכי נעביד:
Rashi on Gittin 5b:20:2.english: Appointed over bills of divorce - For we hold (Kiddushin 6b) that anyone who is not knowledgeable in the nature of divorce documents and betrothals should not have dealings with them, and they would appoint a great man to instruct [people] how we should proceed.

Rashi on Gittin 5b:20:3.english: You are not required - [to stand over each letter], but only over one line.

Rashi on Gittin 5b:2:1.hebrew: בפלוגתא - כי הך פלוגתא דרבה ורבא, איפליגו נמי אמוראי קמאי:
Rashi on Gittin 5b:2:1.english: In the dispute - Like this dispute of Rabba and Rava, the earlier Amoraim also disagreed.

Rashi on Gittin 5b:3:1.english: Brought a bill of divorce - From overseas.

Rashi on Gittin 5b:5:1.hebrew: ותסברא - לא גרסינן. ואי נמי גרסינן ליה, לאו לאורועי "תסתיים" קאתי, דשפיר "תסתיים" דרבי יהושע הוא דאמר "לפי שאין בקיאין". אלא הכי פריך: ותסברא? הא דאמר דיחידי הוה:
Rashi on Gittin 5b:5:1.english: And can you understand - We do not have this reading. And even if we do have it, it does not come to undermine [the Gemara's earlier conclusion] "it can be inferred," for the inference is sound that it is Rabbi Yehoshua who said [the reason is] "because they are not well versed." Rather, this is what it asks: And can you understand that what [the earlier statement] said refers to a single [agent]?

Rashi on Gittin 5b:5:2.hebrew: והא רבה אית ליה דרבא - ובעינן לקיימו:
Rashi on Gittin 5b:5:2.english: But Rabba holds like Rava - And we require that it be authenticated.

Rashi on Gittin 5b:6:1.hebrew: הוה בהדיה - ואמרינן לעיל: בי תרי דמייתו גיטא, מילתא דלא שכיחא:
Rashi on Gittin 5b:6:1.english: He had [another] with him - And we said above that two [people] who bring a get is an uncommon matter.

Rashi on Gittin 5b:7:1.english: In the presence of how many [people] does he give it to her - The agent.

Rashi on Gittin 5b:9:1.hebrew: לפי שאין בקיאין - הלכך בתרי סגי, דלהוו סהדי דאמר שליח "בפני נכתב", ואי אתי בעל תו ומערער, לא משגחינן ביה:
Rashi on Gittin 5b:9:1.english: Because they are not experts - Therefore two [witnesses] suffice, so that they will be witnesses that the agent said, "It was written in my presence"; and if the husband later comes and contests it, we pay no attention to him.

Rashi on Gittin 5b:9:2.hebrew: לפי שאין עדים כו' - וכיון דלקיומי הוא, בעינן תלתא, כדאמרינן בכתובות בפרק שני (דף כא:), דקיום שטרות בשלשה:
Rashi on Gittin 5b:9:2.english: Because there are no witnesses, etc. - And since it is for the sake of ratification, we require three, as we say in Ketubot, in the second chapter (21b), that the ratification of documents [requires] three.

Tosafot on Gittin 5b:10:1.hebrew: הא מדר' יהושע כו' רבי יוחנן סבר לפי שאין עדים מצויין לקיימו - לא בעי לשנויי דסבר כאידך לישנא דפ"ב (לקמן גיטין דף יז.), דההוא לישנא דהתם, דקאמר "שנים אין צריכין לומר 'בפני נכתב'", הוא עיקר, דקאמר עלה: "יתד הוא שלא תמוט". ועוד, דבההיא שינויא לא הוה משני הא דפריך: "והא רבה אית ליה דרבא":
Tosafot on Gittin 5b:10:1.english: "But from [the statement of] Rabbi Yehoshua etc. Rabbi Yochanan holds that [the reason is] because witnesses are not available to ratify it" - [The Gemara] does not want to answer that he holds like the other version [of Rabbi Yochanan's reasoning] in the second chapter (below, Gittin 17a). For that version there, in which it says, "Two do not need to say, 'It was written in our presence,'" is the primary one, about which [the Gemara] says: "It is a peg, so that it will not totter." And furthermore, according to that answer [the Gemara] would not have answered what it asks: "But Rabba holds [the opinion of] Rava."

Tosafot on Gittin 5b:13:1.hebrew: והא קיימא לן דאין עד נעשה דיין ה"מ בדאורייתא כו' - רש"י לא גריס ליה, והדין עמו. דכיון דפשיטא דבדרבנן עד נעשה דיין, כדפריך לבסוף, היכי פריך מעיקרא: "הא קיימא לן דאין עד נעשה דיין"? דהא פשיטא דלא ס"ד דהכא הוי דאורייתא. ומיהו בפרק קמא דכתובות (דף יא.) יש קצת כענין זה גבי גר קטן: מטבילין אותו על דעת ב"ד, ופריך: מאי קמ"ל? תנינא: זכין לאדם שלא בפניו כו'. והדר פריך: והא קי"ל דודאי עבד בהפקירא ניחא ליה: הכי גריס ר"ת: כיון דאשה כשירה להביא את הגט, זימנין דמייתי ליה איתתא. וכן פירש רבינו חננאל. וה"ה דהוה מצי למימר: זימנין דמייתי ליה קרוב:
Tosafot on Gittin 5b:13:1.english: "But we maintain that a witness cannot become a judge"; this applies only to Torah law, etc. - Rashi does not have this reading, and the reasoning is with him. For since it is obvious that in rabbinic law a witness can become a judge, as the Gemara asks at the end, how could it ask at the outset, "But we maintain that a witness cannot become a judge"? For it is obvious that it could not have entered [the Gemara's] mind that here the law is from the Torah. However, in the first chapter of Ketubot (11a) there is something somewhat similar to this regarding a minor convert: "We immerse him on the authority of a court," and [the Gemara] asks: What is [the Mishnah] teaching us? We learned: "One may act on behalf of a person in his absence," etc. And then it asks further: But we maintain that surely a slave is content with [being] ownerless (i.e., set free). Rabbeinu Tam reads it thus: Since a woman is fit to bring the *get*, sometimes a woman brings it. And so Rabbeinu Chananel explained. And the same applies [to others]: [the Gemara] could have said, "sometimes a relative brings it."

Tosafot on Gittin 5b:14:1.hebrew: הכי גריס ר"ת: כיון דאשה כשירה להביא את הגט, זימנין דמייתי ליה איתתא. וכן פירש רבינו חננאל. וה"ה דהוה מצי למימר: זימנין דמייתי ליה קרוב:
Tosafot on Gittin 5b:14:1.english: Rabbeinu Tam reads it this way: "Since a woman is fit to bring the bill of divorce, sometimes a woman brings it." And so Rabbeinu Chananel explained. And likewise [the Gemara] could have said: "Sometimes a relative brings it."

Tosafot on Gittin 5b:17:1.hebrew: כיצד יעשה - פי': כיצד יעשה לרבנן שתינשא לכתחילה, או אם נישאת — שלא תצא. אבל לולד אין צריך תקנה, דבלא תקנה לא הוי ממזר, דלית להו "כל המשנה" כו'. ולר"מ, כיצד יעשה — קודם נישואין; אבל לאחר נישואין מסתבר דלר"מ אין תקנה, דכיון דהולד ממזר, א"כ כל הדרכים האלו בה, ותצא מזה ומזה, וכל הנהו דתנן לקמן בהזורק (גיטין דף פ.):
Tosafot on Gittin 5b:17:1.english: How should he act - Explanation: How should he act, according to the Rabbis, so that she may marry initially, or, if she has [already] married, so that she need not leave [her husband]? But for the offspring no remedy is needed, because without a remedy he is not a mamzer, for they do not hold [the principle of] "Whoever changes..." etc. And according to R. Meir, "How should he act" refers to before the marriage. But after the marriage, it is reasonable that according to R. Meir there is no remedy, since the offspring is a mamzer; if so, all these consequences apply to her, and she must leave this one and that one, and all those [consequences] that we learn below in [the chapter] Hazorek (Gittin 80a).

Tosafot on Gittin 5b:17:2.hebrew: יטלנו הימנה ויחזור ויתננו לה ויאמר כו' - מכאן משמע דצריך לומר בשעת נתינה "בפני נכתב", מדקאמר "יטלנו הימנה". וה"ה לאחר נתינה תוך כדי דיבור דמהני, מדקאמר לעיל שנתנו לה כשהיה פיקח, ולא הספיק לומר "בפני נכתב" עד שנתחרש. אבל לאחר כדי דיבור, מספקא לר"י אי מהני כל זמן שעסוקים באותו ענין או לאו. וקודם נתינה, מספקא לר"י נמי אי מהני. ומדתנן בפרק כל הגט (לקמן גיטין דף כט:): "המביא גט ממדינת הים וחלה, עושה בבית דין שליח ואומר כו'" - אין ראיה, דהרי אומר כשהגט יוצא מתחת ידו:
Tosafot on Gittin 5b:17:2.english: "He should take it from her, and again give it to her, and he should say," etc. - From here it is implied that one must say "It was written in my presence" at the time of giving, since [the baraita] says "he should take it from her." And the same applies to [saying it] after the giving, within the time of a statement [toch kedei dibbur], that it is effective, since [the Gemara] said above that he gave it to her while he was of sound mind, and did not manage to say "It was written in my presence" before he became deaf. But after the time of a statement, Ri is uncertain whether it is effective, as long as they are still engaged in the same matter, or not. And before the giving, Ri is likewise uncertain whether it is effective. And from what we learned in the chapter "Kol HaGet" (later, Gittin 29b): "One who brings a bill of divorce from overseas and falls ill appoints an agent in the court, and he says," etc. - there is no proof, for he says [it] as the bill of divorce leaves his hand.

Tosafot on Gittin 5b:1:1.hebrew: אי בעית אימא טעמא מאי כו' - רש"י לא גריס "איבעית אימא", דסיומא דמילתא הוא. ולר"י נראה דשפיר גריס ליה, ומוקי לה השתא קודם שלמדו דכיון דניסת לא תצא; כיון דלזיוף ליכא למיחש, דנתקיים בחותמיו, וליכא אלא לעז בעלמא דשלא לשמה, אפי' אי אתי בעל ומערער, כדפרישית לעיל (גיטין ה ע"א ד"ה א"ה בעל):
Tosafot on Gittin 5b:1:1.english: "If you wish, say: What is the reason," etc. - Rashi does not read "if you wish, say," for it is the conclusion of the matter. But it appears to Rabbi Yitzchak that it is properly read, and he establishes it [as speaking] now, before they learned that since she married, she does not leave [the marriage]; since there is no need to worry about forgery, for [the bill] was validated through its signatories, and there is only a mere rumor that it was [written] not for her sake, even if the husband comes and contests, as I explained above (Gittin 5a, s.v. "Im kein ba'al"):

Tosafot on Gittin 5b:22:1.hebrew: אפילו לא כתב בו אלא שיטה אחת כו' - פירוש: שלא ראה אלא שיטה ראשונה, דמסתמא סיימו לשמה:
Tosafot on Gittin 5b:22:1.english: "Even if he wrote only one line of it..." - Explanation: [Rabbi Elazar's ruling applies even if the agent] saw only the first line [being written for her sake], since presumably [the scribe] finished it for her sake as well.

Tosafot on Gittin 5b:5:1.hebrew: ותסברא והא רבה אית ליה דרבא - לא גרסינן "ותסברא", כדפירש בקונטרס. ובסמוך, דקאמר: "אלא ר' שמעון בר אבא איניש אחרינא הוה בהדיה", לא גרסינן "אלא", דאינו בא לסתור "תסתיים". ובסמוך נמי קאמר: "הא מדריב"ל סבר לפי שאין בקיאין לשמה" כו':
Tosafot on Gittin 5b:5:1.english: "And can you understand [that]... but Rabbah holds like Rava" - We do not read "And can you understand," as Rashi explained in the Kuntres. And later, where [the Gemara] says: "Rather, R. Shimon bar Abba, another person was with him," we do not read "rather," for it does not come to refute [the proof] "it is concluded." And later too it says: "But from R. Yehoshua ben Levi, who holds that [the rule is] because they are not expert in [writing a bill of divorce] for her sake," etc.
